title: Jump Game
statement:
A delivery drone flies along a straight row of charging pads, numbered 0 to len(nums) - 1. It starts on pad 0. On pad i it can recharge enough to fly forward up to nums[i] pads: to any pad from i + 1 to i + nums[i]. A pad with nums[i] = 0 is a dead end unless the drone can skip past it from an earlier pad.

Write def solution(nums) that returns True if the drone can reach the last pad, and False if not. With one pad, it is already there.

examples.why: The LeetCode 55 example 1. Pad 0 reaches pad 1, and pad 1 reaches pad 4.
The LeetCode 55 example 2. Every pad tops out at pad 3, which has 0.
One pad: the drone starts on the last pad.

think.q: Do you need to find the actual jumps?
think.a: No. You only need a yes or no: is the last pad reachable at all? A jump may be shorter than nums[i], so from pad i every pad up to i + nums[i] is reachable. That means the set of reachable pads is always one solid block starting at pad 0.

From pad 0 you reach up to pad 3. Pad 1 reaches up to 1 + 2 = 3. Pad 2 reaches up to 2 + 1 = 3. Pad 3 reaches 3 + 0 = 3. Every road ends at pad 3, a dead end, so pad 4 is never reached: False. The useful number was the farthest pad reachable so far.

think.q: What is the first idea that works?
think.a: Keep a reachable list. Mark pad 0. For each marked pad i, mark every pad from i + 1 to i + nums[i]. Return whether the last pad is marked. Correct, but long jumps make it O(n x max jump), up to 10^10 steps.

Greedy: track the farthest reach. Because the reachable pads form one block from 0 to far, one number describes the whole set. Scan left to right. If i > far, pad i cannot be reached, and nor can anything after it: return False. Otherwise set far = max(far, i + nums[i]). Once far reaches the last index, return True.

1. far = 0, last = len(nums) - 1.
  2. For each i: if i > far, return False.
  3. Set far = max(far, i + nums[i]). If far ≥ last, return True.
  4. The loop always returns: on the last index, either i > far or far ≥ last. Keep a final return True only as a fallback.

One pad ([0] is True). A zero on pad 0 with more pads (False). A zero you can jump over. A zero on the last pad, which does not matter. Exactly enough reach to land on the last pad. Huge jumps, which make the marking idea slow.

hints: If you can reach pad 5, can you also reach pads 1 to 4? What does that say about the shape of the reachable set?
One number describes everything you can reach: the farthest pad so far. How does pad i extend it?
Scan left to right with far. If i > far you are stuck: return False. Else far = max(far, i + nums[i]), and return True as soon as far ≥ len(nums) - 1.
explain:
Example 1, nums = [2, 3, 1, 1, 4] (last index 4):

  • i = 0: 0 ≤ far (0). far = max(0, 0 + 2) = 2.
  • i = 1: 1 ≤ 2. far = max(2, 1 + 3) = 4 ≥ 4: return True.

Example 2, [3, 2, 1, 0, 4]: far becomes 3 at i = 0 and stays 3 through i = 3, because every pad tops out at 3. At i = 4, 4 > 3: return False.

Why one number is enough: if pad j is reachable, every pad before it is too (you can always fly a shorter hop), so the reachable pads are exactly 0..far. The greedy never has to choose which jump to take. It just records the best reach, in one O(n) pass.
